segments.en: PAUL'S GOSPEL REVEALED BY CHRIST
segments.sw: INJILI YA PAULO ILIFUNULIWA NA KRISTO

segments.en: "For I make known to you, brethren, as touching the gospel which was preached by me, that it is not after man. For neither did I receive it from man, nor was I taught it, but it came to me through revelation of Jesus Christ. For ye have heard of my manner of life in time past in the Jews' religion, how that beyond measure I persecuted the church of God, and made havock of it: and I advanced in the Jews' religion beyond many of mine own age among my countrymen, being more exceedingly zealous for the traditions of my fathers."--GAL. i. 11-14.
segments.sw: "Ndugu zangu, ninawajulisha kwamba injili niliyowahubiria si ya namna ya kibinadamu. Kwa maana sikuipokea kutoka kwa mwanadamu, wala sikufundishwa nayo na mwanadamu, bali ilinijia kwa ufunuo wa Yesu Kristo. Maana mmesikia habari za maisha yangu ya zamani katika dini ya Kiyahudi, jinsi nilivyolitesa kanisa la Mungu kupita kiasi na kuliharibu; nami niliendelea katika dini ya Kiyahudi kuliko wengi wa rika langu katika taifa langu, nikijitahidi sana kushika mapokeo ya baba zangu."--GAL. i. 11-14.

segments.en: Here the Epistle begins in its main purport. What has gone before is so much exordium. The sharp, stern sentences of vv. 6-10 are like the roll of artillery that ushers in the battle. The mists rise from the field. We see the combatants arrayed on either side. In due order and with cool self-command the Apostle proceeds to marshal and deploy his forces. His truthful narrative corrects the misrepresentations of his opponents, and repels their attack upon himself. His powerful dialectic wrests from their hands and turns against them their weapons of Scriptural proof. He wins the citadel of their position, by establishing the claim of the men of faith to be the sons of Abraham. On the ruins of confuted legalism he builds up an impregnable fortress for Christian liberty, an immortal vindication of the gospel of the grace of God.
segments.sw: Hapa ndipo Waraka unapoanza kushughulikia kusudi lake kuu. Yote yaliyotangulia ni utangulizi. Sentensi kali na zenye ukali za mistari ya 6-10 ni kama ngurumo za mizinga zinazoashiria kuanza kwa vita. Ukungu unaondoka kwenye uwanja wa mapambano. Tunaona wapiganaji wakiwa wamejipanga pande zote mbili. Kwa utaratibu mzuri na utulivu wa moyo, Mtume anaanza kuyapanga majeshi yake na kuyaweka katika nafasi zao. Masimulizi yake ya kweli yanasahihisha maelezo potovu ya wapinzani wake na kurudisha nyuma mashambulizi yao dhidi yake mwenyewe. Hoja zake zenye nguvu zinawanyang'anya silaha zao za uthibitisho kutoka katika Maandiko na kuzitumia dhidi yao. Anateka ngome yao kuu kwa kuthibitisha kwamba watu wa imani ndio wana wa Abrahamu. Juu ya magofu ya msimamo uliobatilishwa wa kutegemea sheria, anajenga ngome isiyoweza kutekwa ya uhuru wa Kikristo, utetezi wa kudumu wa injili ya neema ya Mungu.

segments.en: The cause of Gentile freedom at this crisis was bound up with the person of the Apostle Paul. His Gospel and his Apostleship must stand or fall together. The former was assailed through the latter. He was himself just now "the pillar and stay of the truth." If his character had been successfully attacked and his influence destroyed, nothing, humanly speaking, could have saved Gentile Christendom at this decisive moment from falling under the assaults of Judaism. When he begins his crucial appeal with the words, "Behold, I Paul say unto you" (ch. v. 2), we feel that the issue depends upon the weight which his readers may attach to his personal affirmation. He pits his own truthfulness, his knowledge of Christ, his spiritual discernment and authority, and the respect due to himself from the Galatians, against the pretensions of the new teachers. The comparison is not indeed so open and express as that made in 2 Corinthians; none the less it tacitly runs through this Epistle. Paul is compelled to put himself in the forefront of his argument. In the eyes of his children in the faith, he is bound to vindicate his Apostolic character, defamed by Jewish malice and untruth.
segments.sw: Katika kipindi hiki cha hatari, suala la uhuru wa watu wa Mataifa lilihusiana moja kwa moja na nafsi ya Mtume Paulo. Injili yake na utume wake lazima visimame au vianguke pamoja. Injili yake ilishambuliwa kwa kushambulia utume wake. Yeye mwenyewe alikuwa wakati huo "nguzo na msingi wa kweli." Kama tabia yake ingechafiliwa kwa mafanikio na ushawishi wake kuharibiwa, kwa mtazamo wa kibinadamu hakuna kitu ambacho kingeweza kuwaokoa Wakristo wa Mataifa katika wakati huo wa maamuzi wasiangukie chini ya mashambulizi ya dini ya Kiyahudi. Anapoanza ombi lake la maana sana kwa maneno, "Tazama, mimi Paulo nawaambia" (ch. v. 2), tunahisi kwamba matokeo yanategemea uzito ambao wasomaji wake wanaweza kuupa uthibitisho wake binafsi. Anaweka ukweli wake mwenyewe, ujuzi wake wa Kristo, utambuzi na mamlaka yake ya kiroho, na heshima anayostahili kutoka kwa Wagalatia, dhidi ya madai ya walimu wapya. Kwa kweli ulinganisho huu si wa wazi na wa moja kwa moja kama ule unaopatikana katika 2 Wakorintho; hata hivyo unaonekana kwa njia isiyo ya moja kwa moja katika Waraka huu wote. Paulo analazimika kujiweka mwenyewe mbele kabisa katika hoja yake. Mbele ya watoto wake katika imani, ana wajibu wa kuutetea utume wake, ambao umechafuliwa na uovu na uongo wa wapinzani wake wa Kiyahudi.

segments.en: The first two chapters of this Epistle are therefore Paul's Apologia pro vita sua. With certain chapters in 2 Corinthians, and scattered passages in other letters, they form the Apostle's autobiography, one of the most perfect self-portraitures that literature contains. They reveal to us the man more effectively than any ostensible description could have done. They furnish an indispensable supplement to the external and cursory delineations given in the Acts of the Apostles. While Luke skilfully presents the outward framework of Paul's life and the events of his public career, it is to the Epistles that we turn--to none more frequently than this--for the necessary subjective data, for all that belongs to his inner character, his motives and principles. This Epistle brings into bold relief the Apostle's moral physiognomy. Above all, it throws a clear and penetrating light on the event which determined his career--the greatest event in the history of Christianity after the Day of Pentecost--Paul's conversion to faith in the Lord Jesus.
segments.sw: Kwa hiyo sura mbili za kwanza za Waraka huu ni Apologia pro vita sua ya Paulo. Pamoja na sura fulani katika 2 Wakorintho na vifungu vilivyotawanyika katika nyaraka nyingine, zinafanyiza historia ya maisha ya Mtume iliyoandikwa na yeye mwenyewe, mojawapo ya picha kamilifu zaidi za mtu kujieleza mwenyewe katika fasihi. Zinamfunua kwetu kwa ufanisi zaidi kuliko maelezo yoyote ya moja kwa moja yangeweza kufanya. Ni nyongeza ya lazima kwa maelezo ya nje na ya muhtasari yaliyotolewa katika Matendo ya Mitume. Luka anaeleza kwa ustadi muundo wa nje wa maisha ya Paulo na matukio ya huduma yake ya hadharani; lakini tunazigeukia nyaraka zake—na hasa Waraka huu—ili kupata habari za lazima kuhusu maisha yake ya ndani, tabia yake, nia zake na kanuni zake. Waraka huu unaonyesha kwa uwazi mkubwa sura ya maadili ya Mtume. Zaidi ya yote, unatoa mwanga wazi na wenye kupenya juu ya tukio lililoamua mwelekeo wa maisha yake—tukio kubwa zaidi katika historia ya Ukristo baada ya Siku ya Pentekoste—kuongoka kwa Paulo na kumwamini Bwana Yesu.

segments.en: This was at once the turning-point in the Apostle's life, and the birth-hour of his gospel. If the Galatians were to understand his teaching, they must understand this occurrence; they must know why he became a Christian, how he had received the message which he brought to them. They would, he felt sure, enter more sympathetically into his doctrine, if they were better acquainted with the way in which he had arrived at it. They would see how well-justified was the authority, how needful the severity with which he writes. Accordingly he begins with a brief relation of the circumstances of his call to the service of Christ, and his career from the days of his Judaistic zeal, when he made havoc of the faith, till the well-known occasion on which he became its champion against Peter himself, the chief of the Twelve (ch. i. 11-ii. 21.) His object in this recital appears to be threefold: to refute the misrepresentations of the Circumcisionists; to vindicate his independent authority as an Apostle of Christ; and further, to unfold the nature and terms of his gospel, so as to pave the way for the theological argument which is to follow, and which forms the body of the Epistle.
segments.sw: Tukio hilo lilikuwa wakati wa mabadiliko makubwa katika maisha ya Mtume na wakati wa kuzaliwa kwa injili yake. Ili Wagalatia waelewe mafundisho yake, iliwabidi waelewe tukio hili; iliwabidi wajue kwa nini alikua Mkristo na jinsi alivyoupokea ujumbe aliowaletea. Alikuwa na hakika kwamba wangeelewa na kuyakubali mafundisho yake kwa moyo zaidi kama wangejua vizuri njia iliyomfikisha kwenye mafundisho hayo. Wangeona jinsi mamlaka anayotumia katika kuandika ilivyokuwa halali, na jinsi ukali wake ulivyokuwa wa lazima. Kwa hiyo anaanza kwa kusimulia kwa ufupi mazingira ya kuitwa kwake kumtumikia Kristo, na mwenendo wake tangu siku za bidii yake kwa dini ya Kiyahudi, alipokuwa akiharibu imani, hadi tukio linalojulikana sana ambapo akawa mtetezi wake dhidi ya Petro mwenyewe, kiongozi wa wale Kumi na Wawili (ch. i. 11-ii. 21.) Inaonekana kwamba kusudi lake katika masimulizi haya lina sehemu tatu: kubatilisha maelezo ya uongo ya watetezi wa tohara; kuthibitisha mamlaka yake ya kujitegemea akiwa Mtume wa Kristo; na zaidi ya hayo, kufafanua asili na masharti ya injili yake ili kuandaa njia kwa hoja ya kitheolojia itakayofuata, ambayo ndiyo sehemu kuu ya Waraka.

segments.en: I. Paul's gospel was supernaturally conveyed to him, by a personal intervention of Jesus Christ. This assertion is the Apostle's starting-point. "My gospel is not after man. I received it as Jesus Christ revealed it to me."
segments.sw: I. Paulo alipokea injili yake kwa njia isiyo ya kawaida ya kibinadamu, kwa Yesu Kristo mwenyewe kuingilia kati. Dai hili ndilo mwanzo wa hoja ya Mtume. "Injili yangu si ya namna ya kibinadamu. Niliipokea kama Yesu Kristo alivyonifunulia."

segments.en: That the initial revelation was made to him by Christ in person, was a fact of incalculable importance for Paul. This had made him an Apostle, in the august sense in which he claims the title (ver. 1). This accounts for the vehemence with which he defends his doctrine, and for the awful sentence which he has passed upon its impugners. The Divine authorship of the gospel he preached made it impossible for him to temporize with its perverters, or to be influenced by human favour or disfavour in its administration. Had his teaching been "according to man," he might have consented to a compromise; he might reasonably have tried to humour and accommodate Jewish prejudices. But the case is far otherwise. "I am not at liberty to please men," he says, "for my gospel comes directly from Jesus Christ" (vv. 10, 11). So he "gives" his readers "to know," as if by way of formal notification.<sup>14</sup>
segments.sw: Kwamba ufunuo wa kwanza ulitolewa kwake na Kristo mwenyewe kulikuwa jambo lenye umuhimu usiopimika kwa Paulo. Hilo ndilo lililomfanya kuwa Mtume, kwa maana tukufu ambayo anadai cheo hicho (ver. 1). Hilo linaeleza nguvu ya hisia anazotumia kutetea mafundisho yake, na hukumu kali aliyoitoa dhidi ya wanaoyapinga. Kwa sababu Mungu ndiye mwanzilishi wa injili aliyohubiri, haikuwezekana kwake kufanya mapatano na wale walioipotosha, wala kuongozwa na kukubaliwa au kukataliwa na wanadamu katika huduma yake. Kama mafundisho yake yangekuwa "ya namna ya kibinadamu," angeweza kukubali mapatano; angeweza kwa sababu zinazokubalika kujaribu kuwafurahisha Wayahudi na kujipatanisha na mitazamo yao ya awali. Lakini hali ni tofauti kabisa. "Sina uhuru wa kuwapendeza wanadamu," asema, "kwa maana injili yangu inatoka moja kwa moja kwa Yesu Kristo" (vv. 10, 11). Kwa hiyo anawajulisha wasomaji wake, kana kwamba anawapa taarifa rasmi.<sup>14</sup>

segments.en: <sup>14</sup> Comp. Rom. ix. 22; 1 Cor. xii. 3; xv. 1; 2 Cor. viii. 1.
segments.sw: <sup>14</sup> Ling. Rum. ix. 22; 1 Kor. xii. 3; xv. 1; 2 Kor. viii. 1.

segments.en: The gospel of Paul was inviolable, then, because of its superhuman character. And this character was impressed upon it by its superhuman origin: "not according to man, for neither from man did I receive it, nor was I taught it, but by a revelation of Jesus Christ." The Apostle's knowledge of Christianity did not come through the ordinary channel of tradition and indoctrination; Jesus Christ had, by a miraculous interposition, taught him the truth about Himself. He says, "Neither did I," with an emphasis that points tacitly to the elder Apostles, whom he mentions a few sentences later (ver. 17). To this comparison his adversaries forced him, making use of it as they freely did to his disparagement.15 But it comes in by implication rather than direct assertion. Only by putting violence upon himself, and with strong expressions of his unworthiness, can Paul be brought to set his official claims in competition with those of the Twelve. Notwithstanding, it is perfectly clear that he puts his ministry on a level with theirs. He is no Apostle at second-hand, no disciple of Peter's or dependant of the "pillars" at Jerusalem. "Neither did I," he declares, "any more than they, take my instructions from other lips than those of Jesus our Lord."
segments.sw: Kwa hiyo injili ya Paulo haikupaswa kubadilishwa, kwa sababu asili yake ilikuwa juu ya uwezo wa kibinadamu. Sifa hii ilitokana na chanzo chake kilichozidi uwezo wa mwanadamu: "si ya namna ya kibinadamu, kwa maana sikuipokea kutoka kwa mwanadamu, wala sikufundishwa, bali kwa ufunuo wa Yesu Kristo." Ujuzi wa Mtume kuhusu Ukristo haukutokana na njia ya kawaida ya kupokea mapokeo na kufundishwa; Yesu Kristo, kwa kuingilia kati kwa muujiza, alimfundisha kweli inayomhusu yeye mwenyewe. Anasema, "Wala mimi sikuipokea," kwa mkazo unaoelekeza kwa njia isiyo ya moja kwa moja kwa Mitume waliomtangulia, ambao anawataja katika sentensi chache zinazofuata (ver. 17). Wapinzani wake walimlazimisha kufanya ulinganisho huu, kwa kuwa waliutumia bila kusita kumshusha hadhi.15 Lakini ulinganisho huo unaingizwa kwa kudokezwa badala ya kutamkwa moja kwa moja. Ni kwa kujilazimisha sana na kutoa kauli zenye nguvu juu ya kutostahili kwake ndipo Paulo anaweza kuweka madai yake ya mamlaka ya utume katika ushindani na yale ya wale Kumi na Wawili. Hata hivyo, ni wazi kabisa kwamba anaiweka huduma yake katika kiwango kimoja na yao. Yeye si Mtume aliyepokea utume kupitia kwa mtu mwingine, wala si mwanafunzi wa Petro au mtegemezi wa "nguzo" za Yerusalemu. "Wala mimi," anatangaza, "kama wao pia, sikupokea maagizo yangu kutoka katika kinywa kingine isipokuwa cha Yesu Bwana wetu."

segments.en: <sup>15</sup> See ch. ii. 6-14; 1 Cor. i. 12; iii. 22; iv. 9; ix. 1-5; xv. 8-10.
segments.sw: <sup>15</sup> Tazama ch. ii. 6-14; 1 Kor. i. 12; iii. 22; iv. 9; ix. 1-5; xv. 8-10.

segments.en: But what of this "revelation of Jesus Christ," on which Paul lays so much stress? Does he mean a revelation made by Christ, or about Christ? Taken by itself, the expression, in Greek as in English, bears either interpretation. In favour of the second construction--viz. that Paul speaks of a revelation by which Christ was made known to him--the language of ver. 16 is adduced: "It pleased God to reveal His Son in me." Paul's general usage points in the same direction. With him Christ is the object of manifestation, preaching, and the like. 2 Cor. xii. 1 is probably an instance to the contrary: "I will come to visions and revelations of the Lord."16 But it should be observed that wherever this genitive is objective (a revelation revealing Christ), God appears in the context, just as in ver. 16 below, to Whom the authorship of the revelation is ascribed. In this instance, the gospel is the object revealed; and Jesus Christ, in contrast with man, is claimed for its Author. So at the outset (ver. 1) Christ, in His Divine character, was the Agent by whom Paul, as veritably as the Twelve, had received his Apostleship. We therefore assent to the ordinary view, reading this passage in the light of the vision of Jesus thrice related in the Acts.17 We understand Paul to say that no mere man imparted to him the gospel he preached, but Jesus Christ revealed it.
segments.sw: Lakini tunaelewaje huu "ufunuo wa Yesu Kristo," ambao Paulo anauwekea mkazo mkubwa hivyo? Je, anamaanisha ufunuo uliotolewa na Kristo, au ufunuo kuhusu Kristo? Usemi huo ukichukuliwa peke yake, katika Kiyunani kama ilivyo katika Kiingereza, unaruhusu tafsiri zote mbili. Kutetea ufafanuzi wa pili—yaani, kwamba Paulo anazungumzia ufunuo ambao kwa njia yake Kristo alijulikana kwake—maneno ya mstari wa 16 yanatolewa kama ushahidi: "Mungu alipendezwa kumfunua Mwanawe ndani yangu." Matumizi ya kawaida ya Paulo yanaelekeza upande huo huo. Kwake Kristo ndiye mlengwa wa kudhihirishwa, kuhubiriwa na mambo yanayofanana na hayo. Huenda 2 Kor. xii. 1 ni mfano wa kinyume chake: "Nitafikia maono na mafunuo ya Bwana."16 Lakini inapaswa kuzingatiwa kwamba popote ambapo hali hii ya kimilikishi (genitive) inamhusu mlengwa (yaani, ufunuo unaomfunua Kristo), Mungu hutajwa katika muktadha, kama katika mstari wa 16 hapa chini, kuwa ndiye mwanzilishi wa ufunuo huo. Katika tukio hili, injili ndiyo inayofunuliwa; na Yesu Kristo, tofauti na mwanadamu, anatajwa kuwa Mwanzilishi wake. Vivyo hivyo mwanzoni (ver. 1), Kristo katika hali yake ya kimungu ndiye aliyekuwa Mtendaji ambaye kupitia kwake Paulo, kwa hakika sawa na wale Kumi na Wawili, alipokea utume wake. Kwa hiyo tunakubaliana na ufafanuzi wa kawaida, tukisoma kifungu hiki kwa kuzingatia maono ya Yesu yanayosimuliwa mara tatu katika Matendo.17 Tunaelewa kwamba Paulo anasema kwamba si mwanadamu wa kawaida aliyempa injili aliyohubiri, bali Yesu Kristo ndiye aliyeifunua.

segments.en: 16 This genitive is, however, open to the other construction, which is unquestionable in 1 Cor. i. 7; 2 Thess. i. 7; also 1 Pet. i. 7, 13. Rev. i. 1 furnishes a prominent example of the subjective genitive.
segments.sw: 16 Hata hivyo, hali hii ya kimilikishi inaruhusu ufafanuzi mwingine, ambao hauna shaka katika 1 Kor. i. 7; 2 The. i. 7; pia 1 Pet. i. 7, 13. Ufu. i. 1 hutoa mfano ulio wazi wa hali ya kimilikishi inayomhusu mtendaji.

segments.en: <sup>17</sup> Acts ix. 1-19; xxii. 5-16; xxvi. 12-18.
segments.sw: <sup>17</sup> Mdo. ix. 1-19; xxii. 5-16; xxvi. 12-18.

segments.en: On the Damascus road the Apostle Paul found his mission. The vision of the glorified Jesus made him a Christian, and an Apostle. The act was a revelation--that is, in New Testament phrase, a supernatural, an immediately Divine communication of truth. And it was a revelation not conveyed in the first instance, as were the ordinary prophetic inspirations, through the Spirit; "Jesus Christ," in His Divine-human person, made Himself known to His persecutor. Paul had "seen that Just One and heard a voice from His mouth."
segments.sw: Katika njia ya Dameski Mtume Paulo alipata utume wake. Maono ya Yesu aliyetukuzwa yalimfanya kuwa Mkristo na Mtume. Tukio hilo lilikuwa ufunuo—yaani, kwa usemi wa Agano Jipya, utoaji wa kweli kwa njia isiyo ya kawaida na moja kwa moja kutoka kwa Mungu. Nao ulikuwa ufunuo ambao mwanzoni haukutolewa kupitia Roho kama ilivyo kwa uvuvio wa kawaida wa manabii; "Yesu Kristo," katika nafsi yake yenye hali ya kimungu na ya kibinadamu, alijitambulisha kwa mtesaji wake. Paulo alikuwa "amemwona yule Mwenye Haki na kusikia sauti kutoka kinywani mwake."

segments.en: The appearance of Jesus to Saul of Tarsus was in itself a gospel, an earnest of the good tidings he was to convey to the world. "Why persecutest thou Me?" that Divine voice said, in tones of reproach, yet of infinite pity. The sight of Jesus the Lord, meeting Saul's eyes, revealed His grace and truth to the persecutor's heart. He was brought in a moment to the obedience of faith; he said, "Lord, what wilt Thou have me to do?" He "confessed with his mouth the Lord Jesus"; he "believed in his heart that God had raised Him from the dead." It was true, after all, that "God had made" the crucified Nazarene "both Lord and Christ;" for this was He!
segments.sw: Kuonekana kwa Yesu kwa Sauli wa Tarso kulikuwa kwenyewe injili, dhamana ya habari njema ambayo angeipeleka ulimwenguni. "Kwa nini unanitesa?" sauti hiyo ya kimungu ilisema kwa sauti ya lawama, lakini yenye huruma isiyo na kikomo. Kumwona Yesu Bwana, akikutana na macho ya Sauli, kulifunua neema na kweli yake katika moyo wa mtesaji huyo. Mara moja aliletwa kwenye utii wa imani; akasema, "Bwana, unataka nifanye nini?" Alimkiri Bwana Yesu kwa kinywa chake; aliamini moyoni mwake kwamba Mungu alimfufua kutoka kwa wafu. Kumbe ilikuwa kweli kwamba Mungu alikuwa amemfanya Mnazareti aliyesulubiwa kuwa Bwana na Kristo; maana huyu ndiye yeye!

segments.en: The cross, which had been Saul's stumbling-block, deeply affronting his Jewish pride, from this moment was transformed. The glory of the exalted Redeemer cast back its light upon the tree of shame. The curse of the Law visibly resting upon Him, the rejection of men, marked Him out as God's chosen sacrifice for sin. This explanation at once presented itself to an instructed and keenly theological mind like Saul's, so soon as it was evident that Jesus was not accursed, as he had supposed, but approved by God. So Paul's gospel was given him at a stroke. Jesus Christ dying for our sins, Jesus Christ living to save and to rule--behold "the good news"! The Apostle had it on no less authority than that of the risen Saviour. From Him he received it to publish wide as the world.
segments.sw: Msalaba, uliokuwa kikwazo kwa Sauli na uliokuwa umeijeruhi sana fahari yake ya Kiyahudi, ulibadilishwa kuanzia wakati huu. Utukufu wa Mkombozi aliyeinuliwa uliangaza tena juu ya mti wa aibu. Laana ya Sheria iliyokuwa wazi juu yake na kukataliwa kwake na wanadamu vilimtambulisha kuwa dhabihu ya dhambi iliyochaguliwa na Mungu. Mara tu ilipoonekana wazi kwamba Yesu hakuwa amelaaniwa kama Sauli alivyodhani, bali alikuwa amekubaliwa na Mungu, ufafanuzi huu ulimjia mara moja mtu mwenye elimu na akili makini ya kitheolojia kama Sauli. Hivyo Paulo alipewa injili yake kwa wakati mmoja. Yesu Kristo akifa kwa ajili ya dhambi zetu, Yesu Kristo akiishi ili kuokoa na kutawala—tazama "habari njema"! Mtume alikuwa ameipokea kwa mamlaka isiyopungua ile ya Mwokozi aliyefufuka. Kutoka kwake aliipokea ili kuitangaza ulimwenguni kote.

segments.en: Thus Saul of Tarsus was born again. And with the Christian man, the Christian thinker, the theologian, was born in him. The Pauline doctrine has its root in Paul's conversion. It was a single, organic growth, the seed of which was this "revelation of Jesus Christ." Its creative impulse was given in the experience of the memorable hour, when "God who said, Light shall shine out of darkness, in the face of Jesus Christ shined" into Saul's heart. As the light of this revelation penetrated his spirit, he recognised, step by step, the fact of the resurrection, the import of the crucifixion, the Divinity of Jesus, His human mediatorship, the virtue of faith, the office of the Holy Spirit, the futility of Jewish ritual and works of law, and all the essential principles of his theology. Given the genius of Saul and his religious training, and the Pauline system of doctrine was, one might almost say, a necessary deduction from the fact of the appearance to him of the glorified Jesus. If that form of celestial splendour was Jesus, then He was risen indeed; then He was the Christ; He was, as He affirmed, the Son of God. If He was Lord and Christ, and yet died by the Father's will on the cross of shame, then His death could only be a propitiation, accepted by God, for the sins of men, whose efficacy had no limit, and whose merit left no room for legal works of righteousness. If this Jesus was the Christ, then the assumptions of Saul's Judaism, which had led him into blasphemous hatred and outrage towards Him, were radically false; he will purge himself from the "old leaven," that his life may become "a new lump." From that moment a world of life and thought began for the future Apostle, the opposite in all respects of that in which hitherto he had moved. "The old things," he cries, "passed away; lo, they have become new" (2 Cor. v. 17). Paul's conversion was as complete as it was sudden.
segments.sw: Hivyo Sauli wa Tarso alizaliwa upya. Na pamoja na mtu Mkristo, ndani yake alizaliwa pia mwanafikra Mkristo, mwanatheolojia. Mafundisho ya Paulo yana mzizi wake katika kuongoka kwake. Yalikua kwa umoja kama kiumbe hai, na mbegu yake ilikuwa huu "ufunuo wa Yesu Kristo." Msukumo wake wa kuanzisha mambo mapya ulitolewa katika tukio la saa ile isiyosahaulika, wakati Mungu aliyesema kwamba nuru itang'aa kutoka gizani alipoangaza ndani ya moyo wa Sauli katika uso wa Yesu Kristo. Nuru ya ufunuo huu ilipopenya katika roho yake, alitambua hatua kwa hatua ukweli wa ufufuo, maana ya kusulubiwa, uungu wa Yesu, huduma yake ya upatanishi akiwa mwanadamu, nguvu ya imani, kazi ya Roho Mtakatifu, ubatili wa taratibu za dini ya Kiyahudi na matendo ya sheria, pamoja na kanuni zote za msingi za theolojia yake. Tukizingatia akili ya kipekee ya Sauli na mafunzo yake ya kidini, tunaweza karibu kusema kwamba mfumo wa mafundisho ya Paulo ulikuwa hitimisho la lazima kutokana na ukweli kwamba Yesu aliyetukuzwa alikuwa amemtokea. Ikiwa mtu huyo mwenye utukufu wa mbinguni alikuwa Yesu, basi alikuwa amefufuka kweli; basi alikuwa Kristo; alikuwa, kama alivyothibitisha mwenyewe, Mwana wa Mungu. Ikiwa alikuwa Bwana na Kristo, lakini akafa kwa mapenzi ya Baba juu ya msalaba wa aibu, basi kifo chake kilikuwa lazima kiwe dhabihu ya upatanisho kwa ajili ya dhambi za wanadamu, iliyokubaliwa na Mungu, ambayo ufanisi wake haukuwa na kikomo na ambayo thamani yake haikuacha nafasi kwa matendo ya haki yanayotegemea sheria. Ikiwa Yesu huyu alikuwa Kristo, basi misingi ya dini ya Kiyahudi ya Sauli, iliyomwongoza kwenye chuki ya kukufuru na matendo ya ukatili dhidi yake, ilikuwa potovu tangu mizizi yake; atajitakasa na "chachu ya zamani" ili maisha yake yawe "donge jipya." Kuanzia wakati huo ulimwengu mpya wa maisha na mawazo ulianza kwa yule ambaye angekuwa Mtume, kinyume kwa kila namna na ule ambao alikuwa ameishi ndani yake hadi wakati huo. "Mambo ya kale," anasema kwa sauti, "yamepita; tazama, yamekuwa mapya" (2 Kor. v. 17). Kuongoka kwa Paulo kulikuwa kamili kama kulivyokuwa kwa ghafula.

segments.en: This intimate relation of doctrine and experience gives to Paul's teaching a peculiar warmth and freshness, a vividness of human reality which it everywhere retains, despite its lofty intellectualism and the scholastic form in which it is largely cast. It is theology alive, trembling with emotion, speaking words like flames, forming dogmas hard as rock, that when you touch them are yet glowing with the heat of those central depths of the human spirit from which they were cast up. The collision of the two great Apostles at Antioch shows how the strength of Paul's teaching lay in his inward realization of the truth. There was life behind his doctrine. He was, and for the time the Jewish Apostle was not, acting and speaking out of the reality of spiritual conviction, of truth personally verified. Of the Apostle Paul above all divines the saying is true, Pectus facit theologum. And this personal knowledge of Christ, "the master light of all his seeing," began when on the way to Damascus his eyes beheld Jesus our Lord. His farewell charge to the Church through Timothy (2 Tim. i. 9-12), while referring to the general manifestation of Christ to the world, does so in language coloured by the recollection of the peculiar revelation made at the beginning to himself: "God," he says, "called us with a holy calling, according to His purpose and grace, which hath now been manifested by the appearing18 of our Saviour Christ Jesus, who abolished death and brought life and immortality to light19 through the gospel, whereunto I was appointed a preacher and apostle. For which cause I also suffer these things. But I am not ashamed: for I know Him in whom I have believed." This manifestation of the celestial Christ shed its brightness along all his path.
segments.sw: Uhusiano huu wa karibu kati ya mafundisho na uzoefu unayapa mafundisho ya Paulo uchangamfu na upya wa kipekee, na hisia hai ya uhalisi wa maisha ya mwanadamu ambayo yanaihifadhi kila mahali, licha ya kiwango chake cha juu cha kufikiri na muundo wa kielimu ambao kwa kiasi kikubwa yametolewa ndani yake. Ni theolojia iliyo hai, inayotetemeka kwa hisia, inayosema maneno kama miali ya moto, na inayounda mafundisho thabiti kama mwamba ambayo unapoyagusa bado yanawaka kwa joto la vilindi vya ndani kabisa vya roho ya mwanadamu ambamo yalitoka. Mgongano kati ya Mitume hao wawili wakubwa huko Antiokia unaonyesha jinsi nguvu ya mafundisho ya Paulo ilivyokuwa katika utambuzi wake wa ndani wa kweli. Kulikuwa na uhai nyuma ya mafundisho yake. Yeye alikuwa akitenda na kusema kutokana na uhalisi wa imani yake ya kiroho, ya kweli ambayo alikuwa ameithibitisha binafsi, jambo ambalo kwa wakati huo Mtume wa Kiyahudi hakuwa akifanya. Zaidi ya wanatheolojia wote, msemo huu ni wa kweli kuhusu Mtume Paulo: Pectus facit theologum. Na kumjua Kristo binafsi huku, "nuru kuu iliyoongoza yote aliyoyaona," kulianza pale macho yake yalipomwona Yesu Bwana wetu njiani kwenda Dameski. Wosia wake wa mwisho kwa Kanisa kupitia Timotheo (2 Tim. i. 9-12), ingawa unazungumzia kudhihirishwa kwa Kristo kwa ulimwengu wote, unafanya hivyo kwa lugha iliyoathiriwa na kumbukumbu ya ufunuo wa pekee aliopokea mwanzoni: "Mungu," anasema, "alituita kwa wito mtakatifu, kwa kusudi lake mwenyewe na neema yake, ambayo sasa imedhihirishwa kwa kuonekana18 kwa Mwokozi wetu Kristo Yesu, aliyeondoa mauti na kuleta uzima na kutokufa kwenye nuru19 kwa njia ya injili, ambayo kwa ajili yake mimi niliwekwa kuwa mhubiri na mtume. Kwa sababu hiyo ninateseka pia mambo haya. Lakini sioni haya; maana namjua yeye niliyemwamini." Kudhihirishwa huku kwa Kristo wa mbinguni kuliangaza njia yake yote.

segments.en: <sup>18</sup> Ἐπιφανεία, a supernatural appearance, such as that of the Second Advent.
segments.sw: <sup>18</sup> Ἐπιφανεία, kuonekana kwa namna ipitayo uwezo wa kibinadamu, kama kutokea kwake wakati wa Kuja kwa Pili.

segments.en: <sup>19</sup> Φωτίζω, comp. 2 Cor. iv. 6.
segments.sw: <sup>19</sup> Φωτίζω, ling. 2 Kor. iv. 6.

segments.en: II. His assertion of the Divine origin of his doctrine Paul sustains by referring to the previous course of his life. There was certainly nothing in that to account for his preaching Christ crucified. "For you have heard," he continues, "of my manner of life aforetime, when I followed Judaism."
segments.sw: II. Paulo anaunga mkono dai lake kwamba mafundisho yake yana chanzo cha kimungu kwa kurejelea mwenendo wake wa zamani. Kwa hakika hakukuwa na chochote katika mwenendo huo kilichoweza kueleza kwa nini alikuwa akimhubiri Kristo aliyesulubiwa. "Maana mmesikia," anaendelea, "habari za mwenendo wangu wa zamani, nilipofuata dini ya Kiyahudi."

segments.en: Here ends the chain of fors reaching from ver. 10 to 13--a succession of explanations linking Paul's denunciation of the Christian Judaizers to the fact that he had himself been a violent anti-Christian Judaist. The seeming contradiction is in reality a consistent sequence. Only one who had imbibed the spirit of legalism as Saul of Tarsus had done, could justly appreciate the hostility of its principles to the new faith, and the sinister motives actuating the men who pretended to reconcile them. Paul knew Judaism by heart. He understood the sort of men who opposed him in the Gentile Churches. And if his anathema appear needlessly severe, we must remember that no one was so well able to judge of the necessities of the case as the man who pronounced it.
segments.sw: Hapa unamalizika mfululizo wa maneno kwa maana kuanzia mstari wa 10 hadi wa 13—mfululizo wa maelezo unaounganisha shutuma za Paulo dhidi ya Wakristo waliotaka kuwalazimisha wengine kufuata desturi za Kiyahudi na ukweli kwamba yeye mwenyewe alikuwa mfuasi mkali wa dini ya Kiyahudi aliyepinga Ukristo. Jambo linaloonekana kuwa la kujipinga kwa kweli ni mfuatano wenye mantiki. Ni mtu aliyekuwa amejazwa na roho ya kutegemea sheria kama Sauli wa Tarso tu ambaye angeweza kutambua kwa usahihi uadui wa kanuni zake dhidi ya imani mpya, na nia mbaya zilizowasukuma watu waliodai kuwa wanaweza kuzipatanisha. Paulo aliijua dini ya Kiyahudi kwa undani. Alielewa aina ya watu waliompinga katika Makanisa ya watu wa Mataifa. Na ikiwa laana yake inaonekana kuwa kali kupita kiasi, tunapaswa kukumbuka kwamba hakuna mtu aliyekuwa na uwezo wa kutathmini vizuri zaidi mahitaji ya hali hiyo kuliko yule aliyeitamka.

segments.en: "You have heard"--from whom? In the first instance, probably, from Paul himself. But on this matter, we may be pretty sure, his opponents would have something to say. They did not scruple to assert that he "still preached circumcision"<sup>20</sup> and played the Jew even now when it suited him, charging him with insincerity. Or they might say, "Paul is a renegade. Once the most ardent of zealots for Judaism, he has passed to the opposite extreme. He is a man you cannot trust. Apostates are proverbially bitter against their old faith." In these and in other ways Paul's Pharisaic career was doubtless thrown in his teeth.
segments.sw: "Mmesikia"—kutoka kwa nani? Pengine mwanzoni kutoka kwa Paulo mwenyewe. Lakini kuhusu jambo hili, tunaweza kuwa na hakika kwamba wapinzani wake wangekuwa na la kusema. Hawakusita kudai kwamba bado "alihubiri tohara"<sup>20</sup> na alijifanya Myahudi hata wakati huo ilipomfaa, wakimshtaki kwa kutokuwa mnyofu. Au wangesema, "Paulo ni msaliti wa imani yake. Wakati mmoja alikuwa mwenye bidii zaidi miongoni mwa watetezi wa dini ya Kiyahudi, sasa amekwenda upande wa pili uliokithiri. Ni mtu ambaye huwezi kumwamini. Inajulikana sana kwamba watu wanaoiacha imani yao huwa na uchungu dhidi ya imani yao ya zamani." Bila shaka maisha ya Paulo akiwa Farisayo yalitumiwa kumshambulia kwa njia hizi na nyingine.

segments.en: <sup>20</sup> Ch. v. 11; comp. 1 Cor. ix. 20; Acts xvi. 3; xxi. 20-26; xxiii. 6.
segments.sw: <sup>20</sup> Ch. v. 11; ling. 1 Kor. ix. 20; Mdo. xvi. 3; xxi. 20-26; xxiii. 6.

segments.en: The Apostle sorrowfully confesses "that above measure he persecuted the Church of God and laid it waste." His friend Luke makes the same admission in similar language.<sup>21</sup> There is no attempt to conceal or palliate this painful fact, that the famous Apostle of the Gentiles had been a persecutor, the deadliest enemy of the Church in its infant days. He was the very type of a determined, pitiless oppressor, the forerunner of the Jewish fanatics who afterwards sought his life, and of the cruel bigots of the Inquisition and the Star-chamber in later times. His restless energy, his indifference to the feelings of humanity in this work of destruction, were due to religious zeal. "I thought," he says, "I ought to do many things contrary to the name of Jesus of Nazareth." In him, as in so many others, the saying of Christ was fulfilled: "The time cometh, when whoso killeth you will think that he is offering a sacrifice to God." These Nazarenes were heretics, traitors to Israel, enemies of God. Their leader had been crucified, branded with the extremest mark of Divine displeasure. His followers must perish. Their success meant the ruin of Mosaism. God willed their destruction. Such were Saul's thoughts, until he heard the protesting voice of Jesus as he approached Damascus to ravage His little flock. No wonder that he suffered remorse to the end of his days.
segments.sw: Mtume anakiri kwa huzuni kwamba alilitesa Kanisa la Mungu kupita kiasi na kuliharibu. Rafiki yake Luka anakiri jambo hilohilo kwa lugha inayofanana.<sup>21</sup> Hakuna jaribio la kuficha au kupunguza uzito wa ukweli huu wenye uchungu, kwamba Mtume mashuhuri wa watu wa Mataifa alikuwa mtesaji, adui hatari zaidi wa Kanisa katika siku zake za mwanzo. Alikuwa mfano halisi wa mdhalimu mwenye msimamo mkali na asiye na huruma, mtangulizi wa Wayahudi wenye ushupavu ambao baadaye walitafuta kumwua, na wa watu wakatili wasiovumilia imani tofauti katika Mahakama ya Kuhukumu Uzushi (Inquisition) na mahakama ya Star-chamber katika nyakati za baadaye. Nguvu zake zisizotulia na kutojali hisia za ubinadamu katika kazi hii ya uharibifu zilitokana na bidii ya kidini. "Nilidhani," anasema, "kwamba nilipaswa kufanya mambo mengi kinyume cha jina la Yesu wa Nazareti." Ndani yake, kama ilivyo kwa wengine wengi, maneno ya Kristo yalitimia: "Wakati unakuja ambapo kila mtu atakayewaua atadhani kwamba anamtolea Mungu dhabihu." Wafuasi hawa wa Yesu wa Nazareti walionekana kwake kuwa wazushi, wasaliti wa Israeli, maadui wa Mungu. Kiongozi wao alikuwa amesulubiwa, akiwa amewekewa alama kali zaidi ya kutopendezwa na Mungu. Wafuasi wake walipaswa kuangamizwa. Mafanikio yao yangemaanisha kuanguka kwa mfumo wa dini uliotegemea Musa. Mungu alitaka waangamizwe. Hayo ndiyo yalikuwa mawazo ya Sauli hadi aliposikia sauti ya Yesu ikimpinga alipokaribia Dameski kuliharibu kundi lake dogo. Si ajabu kwamba alisumbuliwa na majuto hadi mwisho wa siku zake.

segments.en: <sup>21</sup> Acts vii. 58; viii. 1-3; ix. 1.
segments.sw: <sup>21</sup> Mdo. vii. 58; viii. 1-3; ix. 1.

segments.en: Saul's persecution of the Church was the natural result of his earlier training, of the course to which in his youth he committed himself. The Galatians had heard also "how proficient he was in Judaism, beyond many of his kindred and age; that he was surpassed by none in zeal for their ancestral traditions." His birth (Phil. iii. 4, 5), education (Acts xxii. 3), temperament, circumstances, all combined to make him a zealot of the first water, the pink and pattern of Jewish orthodoxy, the rising hope of the Pharisaic party, and an instrument admirably fitted to crush the hated and dangerous sect of the Nazarenes. These facts go to prove, not that Paul is a traitor to his own people, still less that he is a Pharisee at heart, preaching Gentile liberty from interested motives; but that it must have been some extraordinary occurrence, quite out of the common run of human influences and probabilities, that set him on his present course. What could have turned this furious Jewish persecutor all at once into the champion of the cross? What indeed but the revelation of Christ which he received at the Damascus gate? His previous career up to that hour had been such as to make it impossible that he should have received his gospel through human means. The chasm between his Christian and pre-Christian life had only been bridged by a supernatural interposition of the mercy of Christ.
segments.sw: Mateso ya Sauli dhidi ya Kanisa yalikuwa matokeo ya kawaida ya mafunzo yake ya awali na njia aliyojitoa kuifuata katika ujana wake. Wagalatia pia walikuwa wamesikia jinsi alivyofanya maendeleo katika dini ya Kiyahudi kuliko wengi wa kabila na rika lake, na kwamba hakuna aliyemzidi kwa bidii ya kushika mapokeo ya mababu zao. Kuzaliwa kwake (Flp. iii. 4, 5), elimu yake (Mdo. xxii. 3), tabia yake ya asili na mazingira yake yote yalichangia kumfanya kuwa mwenye bidii ya hali ya juu kabisa, mfano bora wa imani ya Kiyahudi iliyofuata mafundisho yanayokubalika, tumaini lililokuwa likichipuka la kundi la Mafarisayo, na chombo kilichofaa sana kukandamiza kundi la Wanazareti lililochukiwa na kuonekana kuwa hatari. Mambo haya hayathibitishi kwamba Paulo ni msaliti wa watu wake mwenyewe, wala kwamba moyoni mwake bado ni Farisayo anayehubiri uhuru wa watu wa Mataifa kwa maslahi yake binafsi; badala yake yanathibitisha kwamba lazima kulikuwa na tukio la ajabu, lililokuwa nje kabisa ya mwenendo wa kawaida wa ushawishi na uwezekano wa kibinadamu, lililomwezesha kufuata njia yake ya sasa. Ni nini ambacho kingeweza kumbadilisha ghafula mtesaji huyu mkali wa Kiyahudi na kumfanya mtetezi wa msalaba? Hakika ni nini kingine isipokuwa ufunuo wa Kristo alioupokea kwenye lango la Dameski? Mwenendo wake wa zamani hadi saa hiyo ulikuwa wa namna ambayo ilifanya isiwezekane kwake kupokea injili yake kwa njia za kibinadamu. Pengo kubwa kati ya maisha yake ya Kikristo na yale ya kabla ya Ukristo liliweza kuvukwa tu kwa rehema ya Kristo kuingilia kati kwa njia ya kimiujiza.

segments.en: Our modern critics, however, think that they know Paul better than he knew himself. They hold that the problem raised by this passage is capable of a natural solution. Psychological analysis, we are told, sets the matter in a different light. Saul of Tarsus had a tender conscience. Underneath his fevered and ambitious zeal, there lay in the young persecutor's heart a profound misgiving, a mortifying sense of his failure, and the failure of his people, to attain the righteousness of the Law. The seventh chapter of his Epistle to the Romans is a leaf taken out of the inner history of this period of the Apostle's life. Through what a stern discipline the Tarsian youth had passed in these legal years! How his haughty spirit chafed and tortured itself under the growing consciousness of its moral impotence! The Law had been truly his παιδαγωγός (ch. iii. 24), a severe tutor, preparing him unconsciously "for Christ." In this state of mind such scenes as the martyrdom of Stephen could not but powerfully affect Saul, in spite of himself. The bearing of the persecuted Nazarenes, the words of peace and forgiveness that they uttered under their sufferings, stirred questionings in his breast not always to be silenced. Self-distrust and remorse were secretly undermining the rigour of his Judaic faith. They acted like a "goad" (Acts xxvi. 14), against which he "kicked in vain." He rode to Damascus--a long and lonely journey--in a state of increasing disquiet and mental conflict. The heat and exhaustion of the desert march, acting on a nervous temperament naturally excitable and overwrought, hastened the crisis. Saul fell from his horse in an access of fever, or catalepsy. His brain was on fire. The convictions that haunted him suddenly took form and voice in the apparition of the glorified Jesus, whom Stephen in his dying moments had addressed. From that figure seemed to proceed the reproachful cry which the persecutor's conscience had in vain been striving to make him hear. A flash of lightning, or, if you like, a sunstroke, is readily imagined to fire this train of circumstances,--and the explanation is complete! When, besides, M. Renan is good enough to tell us that he has himself "experienced an attack of this kind at Byblos," and "with other principles would certainly have taken the hallucinations he then had for visions,"<sup>22</sup> what more can we desire? Nay, does not Paul himself admit, in ver. 16 of this chapter, that his conversion was essentially a spiritual and subjective event?
segments.sw: Hata hivyo, wachambuzi wetu wa kisasa wanafikiri kwamba wanamjua Paulo vizuri kuliko alivyojijua mwenyewe. Wanashikilia kwamba tatizo linalotolewa na kifungu hiki linaweza kufafanuliwa kwa sababu za kawaida za kiasili. Tunaambiwa kwamba uchambuzi wa kisaikolojia unaonyesha jambo hilo kwa mtazamo tofauti. Sauli wa Tarso alikuwa na dhamiri nyeti. Chini ya bidii yake yenye msisimko mkubwa na tamaa ya mafanikio, ndani ya moyo wa mtesaji huyo kijana kulikuwa na mashaka makubwa na hisia za aibu kwa kushindwa kwake na kwa kushindwa kwa watu wake kuifikia haki ya Sheria. Sura ya saba ya Waraka wake kwa Warumi ni ukurasa kutoka katika historia ya maisha ya ndani ya Mtume katika kipindi hiki. Ni nidhamu kali namna gani ambayo kijana huyo wa Tarso alikuwa amepitia katika miaka hiyo ya kutegemea sheria! Roho yake yenye kiburi ilikuwa ikifadhaika na kujitesa kadiri ilivyotambua zaidi kutokuwa na uwezo wa kimaadili! Kwa kweli Sheria ilikuwa imekuwa παιδαγωγός yake (ch. iii. 24), mlezi mkali aliyekuwa akimwandaa bila yeye kujua "kwa ajili ya Kristo." Katika hali hii ya akili, matukio kama kuuawa kwa Stefano kwa ajili ya imani yake yalikuwa lazima yamguse Sauli kwa nguvu, hata bila yeye kutaka. Mwenendo wa Wanazareti walioteswa na maneno ya amani na msamaha waliyoyasema katika mateso yao yaliamsha maswali moyoni mwake ambayo hayakuweza kunyamazishwa kila wakati. Kutojiamini na majuto yalikuwa yakidhoofisha kwa siri msimamo mkali wa imani yake ya Kiyahudi. Yalifanya kazi kama "kichokoo" (Mdo. xxvi. 14), ambacho alikuwa akikipiga teke bure. Alisafiri akielekea Dameski—safari ndefu ya upweke—akiwa katika hali ya fadhaa na migongano ya akili iliyozidi kuongezeka. Joto na uchovu wa safari ya jangwani, vikiathiri hali yake ya neva iliyokuwa kwa asili rahisi kusisimka na kuchoka kupita kiasi, viliharakisha kufikia kilele cha hali hiyo. Sauli alianguka kutoka juu ya farasi wake kwa shambulio la homa au hali ya kupoteza uwezo wa kusogeza mwili (catalepsy). Ubongo wake ulikuwa ukiwaka moto. Imani na mawazo yaliyokuwa yakimsumbua ghafla yalichukua umbo na sauti katika mwonekano wa Yesu aliyetukuzwa, ambaye Stefano alikuwa amemwita katika dakika zake za mwisho za maisha. Kutoka kwa umbo hilo ilionekana kutoka sauti ya lawama ambayo dhamiri ya mtesaji huyo ilikuwa imejaribu bure kumfanya aisikie. Ni rahisi kuwazia radi, au ukipenda, kupatwa na joto kali la jua, kukianzisha kikamilifu mfululizo huu wa matukio—na ufafanuzi umekamilika! Zaidi ya hayo, wakati Bw. Renan anapotuambia kwa hisani kwamba yeye mwenyewe "alipatwa na shambulio la namna hii huko Byblos," na kwamba "kwa kanuni tofauti kwa hakika angechukulia maono yake ya udanganyifu ya wakati huo kuwa maono halisi,"<sup>22</sup> ni nini kingine tunachoweza kutaka? Tena, je, Paulo mwenyewe hakiri katika mstari wa 16 wa sura hii kwamba kuongoka kwake kulikuwa hasa tukio la kiroho na la ndani ya nafsi yake?

segments.en: 22 Les Apôtres, p. 180, note 1.
segments.sw: 22 Les Apôtres, p. 180, note 1.

segments.en: Such is the diagnosis of Paul's conversion offered us by rationalism; and it is not wanting in boldness nor in skill. But the corner-stone on which it rests, the hinge of the whole theory, is imaginary and in fatal contradiction with the facts of the case. Paul himself knows nothing of the remorse imputed to him previously to the vision of Jesus. The historian of the Acts knows nothing of it. In a nature so upright and conscientious as that of Saul, this misgiving would at least have induced him to desist from persecution. From first to last his testimony is, "I did it ignorantly, in unbelief." It was this ignorance, this absence of any sense of wrong in the violence he used against the followers of Jesus, that, in his view, accounted for his "obtaining mercy" (1 Tim. i. 13). If impressions of an opposite kind were previously struggling in his mind, with such force that on a mere nervous shock they were ready to precipitate themselves in the shape of an over-mastering hallucination, changing instantly and for ever the current of his life, how comes it that the Apostle has told us nothing about them? That he should have forgotten impressions so poignant and so powerful, is inconceivable. And if he has of set purpose ignored, nay, virtually denied this all-important fact, what becomes of his sincerity?
segments.sw: Huo ndio ufafanuzi wa kuongoka kwa Paulo ambao tunapewa na mtazamo wa urazini; hauna upungufu wa ujasiri wala ustadi. Lakini jiwe la msingi ambalo ufafanuzi huo unalitegemea, jambo ambalo nadharia yote inalitegemea, ni la kuwazia tu na linapingana kabisa na ukweli wa tukio hilo. Paulo mwenyewe hajui chochote kuhusu majuto yanayodaiwa kuwa alikuwa nayo kabla ya maono ya Yesu. Mwandishi wa historia ya Matendo hajui chochote kuyahusu. Kwa mtu mnyofu na mwenye dhamiri makini kama Sauli, mashaka hayo yangemsukuma angalau kuacha mateso. Tangu mwanzo hadi mwisho ushuhuda wake ni kwamba, "Nilifanya hivyo kwa kutokujua, katika kutokuamini." Ni kutokujua huko, kutokuwa na hisia yoyote kwamba alikuwa akikosea katika ukatili alioutumia dhidi ya wafuasi wa Yesu, ambako kwa maoni yake kulieleza kwa nini "alipata rehema" (1 Tim. i. 13). Ikiwa mawazo ya namna iliyo kinyume yalikuwa yakipambana akilini mwake hapo awali, kwa nguvu kiasi kwamba kutokana na mshtuko wa kawaida wa neva yalikuwa tayari kujitokeza kama maono ya udanganyifu yenye nguvu isiyozuilika, yakibadilisha mara moja na milele mkondo wa maisha yake, inakuwaje kwamba Mtume hakutuambia chochote kuyahusu? Haiwezekani kufikiri kwamba angekuwa amesahau hisia zenye uchungu na nguvu kubwa namna hiyo. Na ikiwa kwa makusudi alipuuza, au hata alilikana kwa njia isiyo ya moja kwa moja jambo hili muhimu kuliko yote, je, unyofu wake unabaki wapi?

segments.en: The Apostle was manifestly innocent of any such predisposition to Christian faith as the above theory imputes to him. True, he was conscious in those Judaistic days of his failure to attain righteousness, of the disharmony existing between "the law of his reason" and that which wrought "in his members." His conviction of sin supplied the moral precondition necessary in every case to saving faith in Christ. But this negative condition does not help us in the least to explain the vision of the glorified Jesus. By no psychological process whatever could the experience of Rom. vii. 7-24 be made to project itself in such an apparition. With all his mysticism and emotional susceptibility, Paul's mind was essentially sane and critical. To call him epileptic is a calumny. No man so diseased could have gone through the Apostle's labours, or written these Epistles. His discussion of the subject of supernatural gifts, in 1 Cor. xii. and xiv., is a model of shrewdness and good sense. He had experience of trances and ecstatic visions; and he knew, perhaps as well as M. Renan, how to distinguish them from objective realities.23 The manner in which he speaks of this appearance allows of no reasonable doubt as to the Apostle's full persuasion that "in sober certainty of waking sense" he had seen Jesus our Lord.
segments.sw: Ni wazi kwamba Mtume hakuwa na mwelekeo wowote wa awali kuelekea imani ya Kikristo kama ule ambao nadharia hiyo inamdhania kuwa nao. Ni kweli kwamba katika siku zake za kufuata dini ya Kiyahudi alitambua kushindwa kwake kuifikia haki na kutokuwepo kwa upatano kati ya "sheria ya akili yake" na ile iliyofanya kazi "katika viungo vyake." Kutambua kwake dhambi kulitimiza sharti la kimaadili linalotangulia imani iokoayo katika Kristo kwa kila mtu. Lakini hali hii ya kutambua upungufu wake haitusaidii hata kidogo kufafanua maono ya Yesu aliyetukuzwa. Hakuna mchakato wowote wa kisaikolojia ambao kwa njia yake uzoefu wa Rum. vii. 7-24 ungeweza kujitokeza kama mwonekano wa namna hiyo. Licha ya uzoefu wake wote wa mambo ya kiroho na jinsi alivyoathiriwa kwa urahisi na hisia, akili ya Paulo ilikuwa kimsingi timamu na yenye uwezo wa kuchambua mambo. Kumwita mtu mwenye kifafa ni kumsingizia. Hakuna mtu aliyekuwa mgonjwa kiasi hicho ambaye angeweza kupitia kazi zote za Mtume au kuandika nyaraka hizi. Mjadala wake kuhusu karama zipitazo uwezo wa kawaida wa kibinadamu, katika 1 Kor. xii. na xiv., ni mfano wa utambuzi makini na busara. Alikuwa na uzoefu wa hali za kunyakuliwa katika roho na maono ya msisimko wa kiroho; naye alijua, labda kama Bw. Renan alivyojua, namna ya kutofautisha mambo hayo na hali halisi za nje ya nafsi yake.23 Jinsi anavyozungumzia mwonekano huu haiachi shaka yoyote ya msingi kwamba Mtume alikuwa amesadiki kikamilifu kuwa, akiwa macho na mwenye fahamu timamu, alikuwa amemwona Yesu Bwana wetu.

segments.en: <sup>23</sup> 1 Cor. xiv. 18; 2 Cor. xii. 1-6; Acts xvi. 9; xviii. 8, 9; xxii. 17, 18.
segments.sw: <sup>23</sup> 1 Kor. xiv. 18; 2 Kor. xii. 1-6; Mdo. xvi. 9; xviii. 8, 9; xxii. 17, 18.

segments.en: It was this sensible and outward revelation that led to the inward revelation of the Redeemer to his soul, of which Paul goes on to speak in ver. 16. Without the latter the former would have been purposeless and useless. The objective vision could only have revealed a "Christ after the flesh," had it not been the means of opening Saul's closed heart to the influence of the Spirit of Christ. It was the means to this, and in the given circumstances the indispensable means.
segments.sw: Ufunuo huu wa nje ulioweza kutambuliwa kwa hisi ndio ulioongoza kwenye ufunuo wa ndani wa Mkombozi katika nafsi yake, ambao Paulo anaendelea kuuzungumzia katika mstari wa 16. Bila ufunuo wa pili, ule wa kwanza usingekuwa na kusudi wala manufaa. Maono hayo ya nje yangeweza tu kumfunua "Kristo kwa jinsi ya mwili" kama yasingekuwa njia ya kuufungua moyo uliofungwa wa Sauli kwa ushawishi wa Roho wa Kristo. Yalikuwa njia ya kufanikisha hili, na katika mazingira yale yalikuwa njia ya lazima.

segments.en: To a history that "knows no miracles," the Apostle Paul must remain an enigma. His faith in the crucified Jesus is equally baffling to naturalism with that of the first disciples, who had laid Him in the grave. When the Apostle argues that his antecedent relations to Christianity were such as to preclude his conversion having come about by natural human means, we are bound to admit both the sincerity and the conclusiveness of his appeal.
segments.sw: Kwa historia ambayo "haitambui miujiza," Mtume Paulo lazima aendelee kuwa fumbo. Imani yake katika Yesu aliyesulubiwa inautatanisha mtazamo unaotegemea sababu za kiasili tu kwa kiwango sawa na imani ya wanafunzi wa kwanza, waliokuwa wamemlaza Yesu kaburini. Mtume anapotoa hoja kwamba uhusiano wake wa awali na Ukristo ulikuwa wa namna ambayo haikuruhusu kuongoka kwake kutokee kwa njia za kawaida za kibinadamu, tunawajibika kukubali unyofu wa hoja yake na nguvu yake ya kutoa hitimisho la uhakika.
